克里娜把酒瓶扔出房間。
那女人又惹自己生氣，真不知道當年怎麼看上她的。

連名字都不想提。

她倒在沙發上，扶著額頭，頭隱隱因為酒精發疼。

生活不能再這樣亂下去。
她得徹底跟那個爛女人分手。

ChatGPT
Krina threw the bottle across the room.

It struck the wall with a sharp crack before dropping onto the floor, mercifully intact.

"That woman..."

She didn't even want to say the name.

After another argument, another round of accusations, another night spent wondering how the hell she'd ever fallen for her in the first place, Krina had finally reached the point where even hearing her name felt exhausting.

She sank onto the sofa and pressed two fingers against her temple.

The alcohol had left a dull ache behind her eyes, but not nearly enough to make her forget anything.

Her long red hair had come loose from its usual neat style, spilling over one shoulder as she leaned back. The woman who could walk into a boardroom and make an entire room fall silent now looked thoroughly defeated by a relationship she couldn't seem to control.

'This can't keep going.'

She closed her eyes.

Her life was already a mess. Her work, her temper, her relationship, and whatever remained of her patience had somehow become one enormous pile of problems.

She needed to end it.

Properly this time.

No more arguments. No more getting back together. No more pretending that the next fight would somehow be different from the last one.

Krina opened her eyes and stared at the empty bottle on the floor.

"That's it," she muttered.

She reached for her phone.

Then stopped.

Her expression darkened.

Even after deciding to break up, she still couldn't bring herself to make the call.

"Unbelievable."

She tossed the phone onto the sofa beside her and leaned her head back.

Somewhere outside, the city continued glowing through the windows, completely indifferent to her romantic disaster.

Krina let out a long breath.

For once, she wanted something simple.

Something that didn't hurt.

Something that didn't come with another argument waiting around the corner.

ChatGPT
Krina picked up her phone.

But she didn't call that woman.

Instead, she called the property management center she'd contacted earlier that day.

She was moving out.

The apartment was full of memories she no longer wanted. Memories of the two of them being reckless together, drunken nights when neither of them had any sense of boundaries, ridiculous attempts at things neither of them should have attempted, and stupid declarations of love that had sounded brilliant after midnight.

Now, remembering any of it made her want to throw up.

She wanted none of it.

New apartment. New neighborhood. New neighbors.

A clean slate.

The new place suited her immediately. It was quieter, brighter, and, most importantly, completely untouched by her disastrous relationship.

Krina paid the deposit without hesitation.

Less than two weeks later, she was already settled into her new home.

The first thing she decided to do was obvious.

Celebrate.

Immediately.

She walked into the convenience store downstairs and headed straight for the refrigerators.

A few minutes later, five large glass bottles of beer were sitting in her basket.

She didn't even pretend to care how excessive that looked.

At the register, the cashier glanced at the bottles.

Then at Krina.

Then back at the bottles.

Finally, she looked up at Krina's face again.

The cashier was a pretty young woman with a neat ponytail and a sweet, clean appearance. There was something almost absurdly innocent about the way she stared.

Krina noticed.

So did the cashier.

Their eyes met.

'What a beautiful woman.'

'What a beautiful girl.'

For one strange second, they were thinking exactly the same thing.

Neither of them looked away immediately.

Krina even let out a soft whistle before catching herself.

She immediately stopped, suddenly aware that she probably looked ridiculous.

While the cashier quietly scanned each bottle, Krina's gaze had already settled on the name tag pinned to her uniform.

**Ximuer.**

'Cute name.'

She had no idea why she'd bothered memorizing it.

She simply did.

The next day, Krina returned to the convenience store.

Same amount of beer.

Same time.

The day after that, she did it again.

By the fourth day, Ximuer finally spoke.

"Miss, do you really drink this much by yourself?"

She tried to make her smile look concerned rather than nosy.

Krina raised an eyebrow.

"Miss? How old are you?"

"Twenty-four."

"That's only a few years younger than me." Krina paused, then added, "Krina. Remember that."

"Okay, Ms. Krina."

"God, no. Don't call me 'Ms.' Can't you make me sound a little younger?"

"Yes...!"

Ximuer straightened immediately, looking as though she'd just been given a very important instruction.

Krina stared at her for a second.

Then, despite herself, the corner of her mouth lifted.

On the fifth day, Krina was unbearably restless.

The air conditioning was excellent.

The beer was excellent.

But there was no one lying beside her.

That was not.

Her mind drifted back to that woman.

Back to those nights when Krina only had to call, and she would come running because she knew exactly what Krina needed.

Krina picked up her phone.

She opened her contacts and stared at the woman's number.

"Damn it..."

Her thumb hovered over the screen.

'No. I can't give her the satisfaction again.'

She called anyway.

By midnight, Krina was already in a hotel room.

"You should just admit you can't live without me."

The woman gently ran her fingers through Krina's hair.

"Shut up."

"This is just..." Krina muttered, avoiding her eyes. "An emergency."

"And what's my compensation?"

"No compensation. I've told you before. That's not what our relationship is."

"But I think it is." The woman gave her a knowing smile. "No compensation next time, and I'm not coming."

"You don't have to be so..."

"Then stop calling me." She shrugged. "Three days? Five days? A week? You'll come back."

Her fingers lightly scratched through Krina's hair again.

"Without me scratching that itch for you, you get all restless anyway."

The warmth that had filled the room only moments ago vanished from Krina's expression.

"You're done. You can leave."

The woman blinked.

"That's cold."

She didn't argue. She simply got dressed, straightened her clothes, checked her appearance in the mirror, and left.

The room became quiet again.

Krina sat alone on the edge of the bed.

She stared at the closed door.

'Damn it... I really need to cut this relationship off.'

The sixth day was a Saturday.

Krina showed up at the convenience store again, carrying the same five bottles of beer.

At the register, she set them down one by one.

"...Krina."

Krina slowly looked up.

"You remember my name?"

She knew she looked terrible.

She hadn't slept well, and the previous night's mistake was still sitting heavily in her head. Even the usual sharpness in her expression seemed dulled.

Ximuer hesitated before speaking.

"Drinking this much isn't good for you."

"If I don't drink, it's worse for my health." Krina gave a humorless little laugh. "And worse for my life."

'What a busybody.'

Ximuer lowered her head slightly.

"I had a relative who died of liver cancer."

Her voice was quiet, almost as though she regretted saying it the moment the words left her mouth.

Krina stared at her.

Then she sighed.

"Fine. Now I've got a curse placed on me too. What's the complaint number?"

"No! Don't complain!"

Ximuer immediately looked up, panic flashing across her face.

"This job is really important to me."

"Apologize."

"...I'm sorry."

"Good. Just scan the bottles and let me pay."

Krina took the beer after Ximuer finished scanning everything, paid, and walked away.

Ximuer remained behind the counter.

"..."

She watched Krina's red hair disappear through the automatic doors.

'So cool...'

The call from that woman came out of nowhere.
